title: Krishna's first words: "whence this dejection?" (2.1–2.10)
hook: Krishna's answer to a man in tears is not comfort; it's a jolt, and then Arjuna asks to be taught
tomorrow: The self that is not slain (2.11–2.25)

segments.voice: Yesterday, vishada: Arjuna sat down in his chariot, and chapter one ended. Your line was I can't. Did you say it to someone? Today, Krishna answers. And a look back at the week. Day one hundred sixty-one.

Here's what kindness usually sounds like. A friend is sitting on the floor in tears, saying I can't do this, and someone kneels down, puts a hand on their back, and says: it's okay, you don't have to. Now here's Krishna, with his friend in exactly that state, in the middle of a battlefield. And the first thing he says is closer to: what is this? Where did this come from? Get up. Chapter two begins, and it begins with a jolt.
screen: `A FRIEND ON THE FLOOR, IN TEARS.` → `IT'S OKAY, YOU DON'T HAVE TO.` → `KRISHNA SAYS: GET UP.`

segments.voice: Sanjaya sets the scene: Arjuna, overcome with pity, eyes full of tears. He's already had one line from Krishna, look at them. Now come Krishna's first words of real answer. In Sanskrit: kutas tva kashmalam idam vishame samupasthitam. Older English translators rendered it something like, whence this dejection, at this hour of crisis? Where has this come from, now of all times? Then: klaibyam ma sma gamah Partha. Don't give in to this unmanly weakness. And: tyaktvottishtha parantapa. Cast off this petty faintness of heart and stand up, you who scorch your foes. Stand up. It sounds harsh. But notice what Krishna is doing. He's not agreeing with the story Arjuna is telling about himself. He's reminding him who he is. And it doesn't work, not yet. Arjuna argues again. How can I shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona, who deserve my worship? Better to live as a beggar. I don't even know which is better, winning or losing. And then he says the sentence that turns the whole book: shishyas te 'ham shadhi mam tvam prapannam. I am your student. Teach me. I've come to you for refuge. After that, he says, I will not fight, and he falls silent. And Krishna, between the two armies, answers him, the text says, as if smiling. The jolt wasn't the teaching. The jolt got Arjuna to ask. And that's the week: a camp closed, a book opened, two armies, a request to see, an honest objection, a bow on the floor, and now a student, asking.
screen: `WHENCE THIS DEJECTION?` · `CAST IT OFF AND STAND UP.` · `I AM YOUR STUDENT. TEACH ME.` · `HE ANSWERS, AS IF SMILING.` · then, large: `STAND UP.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: from sitting down to asking. Settle, and breathe. Go back to the bow you set down yesterday, the thing that's too much. You don't have to pick it up. But try a different sentence. Instead of I can't, try: teach me. Say it inside, to God if you pray, or to life, or to your own wiser self. Teach me how to face this. Then just listen, and breathe, and notice what changes in your body when you move from giving up to asking. Imagine someone answering, as if smiling. The bell holds the time.
Uttishtha. Stand up, arise — Krishna's call in Gita two, three. Where has this faintness come from, at this hour? Cast it off, and stand up.
Your line: stand up. Today, when you catch yourself sinking, stand up, literally, and ask one person to teach you something. Day one hundred sixty-one.

screen: `DAY 161 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE SELF THAT IS NOT SLAIN.`

howItsDone: Commentators often treat Gita 2.7, where Arjuna says he is Krishna's student and asks to be taught, as the moment the teaching truly begins, and 2.3's call to cast off faintness and stand up is often quoted in times of discouragement.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Krishna has told you to cast off your weakness and stand up. you still can't. what do you say?
options: I am your student. teach me.
fork.reveal: he argues once more, then says: I am your student, teach me. that sentence starts the whole teaching of the Gita.

original.note: Sanskrit: stand up, arise. Krishna's call in Gita 2.3.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna tells a crying man to toughen up.
what it means: the jolt reminds Arjuna who he is, and it gets him to ask to be taught. then Krishna answers, as if smiling.
what a scholar hears: shishyas te 'ham, I am your student, 2.7. traditional commentators often mark this as where the teaching proper begins.

notes: 'Whence this dejection' is attributed loosely to 'older English translators' (Besant 1895 has 'Whence hath this dejection befallen thee'; Telang 1882 similar). Not quoted as a translation; the validator's list lacks Besant/Telang. Confirm or add to the list.
Klaibya rendered 'unmanly weakness'; some modern readers find the gendered word hard. Confirm wording.
Day 158 calls 'look at these Kurus' (1.25) Krishna's first words in the Gita; this day calls 2.2 his 'first words of real answer'. Confirm consistency with the index title.
Week look-back (155–161) is in the teach. The practice invites 'God if you pray, or life, or your own wiser self'. Confirm tone.
